I've competed in one. LD32. It was pretty rewarding for what it was, and I made a good game but there were a few things I didn't like. First, if you're competing to win, everything has to be fairly instant and lack a certain level of innovation.The player has to have instant access to the game, so web games get the advantage. Players have to get the controls right away, as anything with a slight learning curve gets pass over in an environment where players are trying and judging hundreds of games. Finally the game has to be a certain level of shallow. The more depth, the longer it takes to play and the less likely you are to pick up enough votes to rank. Just some thoughts.
